governance: NT-026 — template changes are Content Design Lead decisions, logged there, never edited here

rule_engine.one_event_one_decision: NT-001 §opening — every module publishes an event; exactly one component (this dispatcher) decides how it is delivered
rule_engine.held_not_dropped: QH-02 — out-of-window service/marketing messages are held
rule_engine.stale_held_discarded: QH-03 — a held message that is stale when the window opens is discarded, not sent late

bd_rules.BD-01: consent_class determines the SMS route — misclassification is a route-suspension risk
bd_rules.BD-02: a marketing message never uses the masking route
bd_rules.BD-03: an order-status message never carries a promotional line — doing so reclassifies the whole message
bd_rules.BD-04: traffic routes through BTRC-listed aggregators only
bd_rules.BD-05: the masking sender ID '1000FiX' registration is tracked in NT-026

fallbacks.sms_undeliverable: retry once, then fall back to the next channel in the matrix (NT-001 §4)
fallbacks.push_not_delivered: fall back to SMS for CH-04 act-now events
fallbacks.email_bounce: flag the address, notify the account owner, fall back to SMS
fallbacks.all_channels_failed: raise an operational task — never silently drop (NT-021)

rule_engine.language_default: bn — language comes from fix.party.preferred_language (MD-013), defaulting to Bengali (PS-03)
rule_engine.sms_segment_warning: Bengali SMS is UCS-2, segmenting at 70 characters, not 160 (CG-010 BC-05)

event_matrix.comment: NT-001 §2.3/§2.4 — W1 rows carry bodies below; later-wave rows carry template IDs only until their wave loads

bodies.comment: W1 lifecycle copy. Status wording is the MD-027 customer-facing column, never the internal state key (T-06). Variables are {{mustache}} with source fields per CG-008 NT-c.
